concepts.title: Linear Pairs of Angles
concepts.definition: A pair of adjacent angles formed by two intersecting lines that lie on a straight line and sum up to 180 degrees.
concepts.key_idea: Adjacent angles on a straight line are supplementary.
question_patterns: find the linear pair partner of an angle of {angle_a} degrees

solution_steps.explain: Since linear pairs sum to 180 degrees, the other angle is found by subtracting the given angle from 180.

concepts.title: Vertically Opposite Angles
concepts.definition: The non-adjacent angles formed directly opposite each other when two straight lines intersect, which are always equal in measure.
concepts.key_idea: Intersecting lines produce equal opposite angles.

solution_steps.explain: Vertically opposite angles are equal, so the opposite angle has the same measure.

concepts.title: Perpendicular Lines
concepts.definition: A pair of intersecting lines that meet at a right angle, making all four angles equal to 90 degrees.
concepts.key_idea: Perpendicular lines intersect at exactly 90 degrees.

solution_steps.explain: Perpendicular lines always intersect at 90 degrees.

concepts.title: Parallel Lines
concepts.definition: Lines on the same plane that never meet or intersect, regardless of how far they are extended in either direction.
concepts.key_idea: Coplanar lines that never intersect are parallel.

concepts.title: Corresponding Angles of Parallel Lines
concepts.definition: Angles in matching relative positions at each intersection where a transversal crosses two parallel lines, which are equal to each other.
concepts.key_idea: Corresponding angles are equal when lines are parallel.

concepts.title: Alternate Interior Angles
concepts.definition: Pairs of angles on opposite sides of a transversal and between the two parallel lines, which are always equal.
concepts.key_idea: Alternate interior angles are equal for parallel lines.

concepts.title: Consecutive Interior Angles
concepts.definition: The interior angles that lie on the same side of the transversal line, which add up to 180 degrees when the lines are parallel.
concepts.key_idea: Interior angles on the same side of a transversal are supplementary.
question_patterns: find the consecutive interior angle to {angle_interior_1} degrees
